$comment: Everything about this repository that the shared pipeline needs and cannot detect. The pipeline itself is identical across every repository that uses it; this file is the only thing that differs, so the workflows and scripts can be distributed byte-for-byte.

identity.description: Turn-key template repository for autonomous, governed software engineering pipelines ('Dark Factory'). Multi-harness agent runner, branch protection, strict verification, and project board delivery.

upstream.$comment: DarkFactory is its own upstream. Consumer repositories set repo to marius-patrik/DarkFactory and pin ref to a commit SHA.

environment.$comment: Detection handles the rest. pyproject.toml here carries only tooling configuration, so the package identity is declared rather than parsed.

areas.$comment: Area labels, commit scopes and agent routing all read this one list, so they cannot drift apart. Declaration order is match order - the first area whose keywords hit wins - so specific areas come before general ones. A consumer repository replaces this block wholesale with its own domains.

agents.description: Harness orchestration, provider adapters, personas, approvals

governance.description: Agent rules, branch protection, required checks, project board taxonomy

release.description: Versioning modes, tagging, asset packaging, release notes

ci.description: GitHub Actions workflows, containers, runner scripts, repository automation

board.$comment: Boards are owned by the account, not by a repository. Every board listed here is linked to this repository so it appears in its Projects tab; the global board aggregates issues from every repository using this pipeline.

pages.$comment: Branch source rather than the Actions build type, so per-pull-request previews can live under pr-<N>/ on the same site. GitHub Pages has exactly one source.
